By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{10}{s}-\frac{1}{s-3},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{5}{s}+\frac{1}{s-3}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{10}{s}-\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =10{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}-{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =10\cdot 1-{e}^{3\cdot t} \\  & =10-{e}^{3t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{5}{s}+\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =5{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =5\cdot 1+{e}^{3\cdot t} \\  & =5+{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10-{e}^{3t} \\ 5+{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

$\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-2}}.
q-331914.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{4{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=-L\{{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=4L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+2L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-3=4{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=-\frac{1}{s+1}.
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)-3=4(-\frac{1}{s+1})+2{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3s-1}{(s+1)(s-2)}.
$$

\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+2L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+4L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-3={X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-2=-{X}_{1}(s)+4{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(s-1){X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s)=3 \\ {X}_{1}(s)+(s-4){X}_{2}(s)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=2-(s-4){X}_{2}(s).
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-1)[2-(s-4){X}_{2}(s)]-2{X}_{2}(s) & =3 \\ 2(s-1)-[(s-1)(s-4)+2]{X}_{2}(s) & =3 \\ -({s}^{2}-5s+6){X}_{2}(s) & =3-2(s-1) \\ -(s-2)(s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =-2s+5 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{2s-5}{(s-2)(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =2-(s-4){X}_{2}(s) \\  & =2-(s-4)\cdot \frac{2s-5}{(s-2)(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{2(s-2)(s-3)-(s-4)(2s-5)}{(s-2)(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{3s-8}{(s-2)(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3s-8}{(s-2)(s-3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{2s-5}{(s-2)(s-3)}.
$$
